specification.problem: Evaluate a single ternary majority gate MAJ3(x1,x2,x3) on an explicit classical input x by building a span-program-derived weighted bipartite graph, compiling its adjacency matrix into a unitary, and running phase estimation to test for an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector with root support. The construction is tiny and explicit, and the abstract's recursive formula evaluation is not covered.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Depth-1 MAJ3 with explicit x compiled into gates, using a concrete span program and graph chosen here as background or assumption, not taken from the abstract. Covers only the single-gate case: no recursive composition, no optimality claim, no query complexity claim. Phase estimation is approximate, and a hard-coded tiny instance is used. Corrects the earlier build: the root state must be prepared explicitly, a consistent vertex encoding is needed, and the edge terms must be implemented by an exact matrix exponential of the whole A, not a Trotterization with mismatched indices.

symbols.meaning: Input vectors, available iff x_i=1. Assumed choice with v_1=(1,1), v_2=(1,-1), v_3=(0,1) is not valid for MAJ3 (v_3 plus v_1 spans, but v_1 and v_2 span too, and the singleton cases need checking). A valid MAJ3 span program must be fixed in a later stage, e.g. a standard one with a 2-dim target space.
Biadjacency matrix: rows are span-space coordinates plus a root row, columns are the available inputs
Root vertex basis state, prepared by explicit X gates on the vertex register
exp(iAs), compiled exactly as a dense unitary for the tiny instance
Probability that the phase register reads 0

equations.label: Graph zero-eigenvector correspondence
equations.description: Evaluation corresponds to a zero-eigenvalue eigenvector of the graph, with root support as the test
equations.abstract_quote: A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph.
equations.justification: The abstract states the correspondence qualitatively. Root support is an assumed refinement, and the detailed graph construction is not given.
assumptions: The root is a dedicated vertex joined to the target row, so the zero eigenvector must have root overlap, not merely lie in the kernel of B

equations.label: Graph unitary
equations.description: Compile the whole adjacency matrix exactly
equations.justification: A standard way to do spectral estimation by phase estimation. The value of s is chosen so that s||A||<pi.
assumptions: Exact dense unitary synthesis for the tiny instance, not Trotterization

equations.label: Zero-bin probability
equations.description: Approximate probability of reading phase 0 in phase estimation on |r>
equations.justification: Standard phase estimation with finite-precision leakage ignored.
assumptions: The smallest nonzero |eigenvalue|·s exceeds the precision

registers.name: vertex
registers.size: ceil(log2 |V|) qubits, with a single flat binary index over all vertices (rows first, then columns)

specification.initial_state: Vertex register prepared in |r> by X gates on the bits of the root index, phase register in |0^m>

steps.description: Fix a verified MAJ3 span program and build B(x) and A(x) with a single flat vertex index. Check that the zero-bin probability separates all 8 inputs by classical spectral simulation.
Prepare |r> on the vertex register, and Hadamards on the phase register.
Apply controlled U^(2^k) from phase qubit k, where each U is the exact exponential of A.
Apply the inverse QFT to the phase register, then read phase 0 externally.

specification.measurement: The phase register is read externally; outcome 0 indicates a zero eigenvector with root support. The returned circuit is measurement-free.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare p_0 against a threshold, which is an assumption. Decode as 1 if p_0 exceeds the threshold.
assumptions: Smallest useful construction: one MAJ3 gate on explicit x
The span program and graph are chosen here and not taken from the abstract
The adjacency matrix is compiled explicitly, with no black-box or query claim
The root-overlap rule and the time s are assumptions
